Section 1 designated the United States Civil Service Commission to exercise, after consultation with the Departments of the Interior and of Health, Education, and Welfare, the President's section 105(i) authority to issue the regulations it describes. Executive Order 12107 section 2-101 (effective January 1, 1979 under its section 2-404; 44 FR 1055) amended the order by substituting the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission, so the delegation continues, amended, with the Office of Personnel Management as the delegate. No held instrument ends it, and the current U.S. Code note prints the section naming the Office of Personnel Management.

Section 2 directed the Civil Service Commission, after consultation, to issue regulations, as it deems appropriate, providing for the establishment, granting and exercise of reemployment rights for employees who leave Federal employment for employment by an Indian tribal organization. Executive Order 12107 section 2-101 (effective January 1, 1979) substituted the Office of Personnel Management for the Commission. The command has no deadline and is tied to the agency's judgment of what is appropriate; no packet source dates its performance, so it is not recorded as exhausted, and the current 5 CFR part 352 authority line in the repository shows the regulations are maintained under this order. No held instrument ends it.

research_rationale:
Identity: Executive Order 11899 of January 22, 1976 (41 FR 3459; FR Doc. 76-2270, filed January 23, 1976), Providing for the Protection of Certain Civil Service Employment Rights of Federal Personnel Who Leave Federal Employment To Be Employed by Tribal Organizations Pursuant to the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act, read in full from the official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11899.txt (the dossier's own-text boundary is verified for the whole order). Four clauses cover it: the recital (authority of section 105(i) of the Act, 5 U.S.C. 3301 and 3 U.S.C. 301); section 1 (the Civil Service Commission is designated to exercise the President's section 105(i) authority to issue regulations for subsections (e)(2) to (e)(4), (f), (g), (h), part of (e)(1), and other civil service rights it finds appropriate); section 2 (the Commission shall, after consultation, issue regulations, as it deems appropriate, on reemployment rights); section 3 (the Secretary of Labor is designated for the section 105(e)(1) regulations, except as provided in section 1). The machine inventory is confirmed without correction. Later instruments: (1) Executive Order 12107 of December 28, 1978 (44 FR 1055), section 2-101, amends and revises each order listed in it, including Executive Order 11899, by substituting Office of Personnel Management for Civil Service Commission and Director, Office of Personnel Management for the Chairman and Commissioners; section 2-404 makes the order effective January 1, 1979, so that date is used. It is a strike-and-insert style substitution, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 the clauses continue, amended, with the Office of Personnel Management as the actor in sections 1 and 2. (2) Executive Order 12608 of September 9, 1987 (52 FR 34617), section 27, amends the recital by replacing the statutory citation text for section 105(i); it states no separate effective date, so its signing date is used, and it changes no command. Both are listed as later events. Ending search: the order has no sunset, duration or terminating condition. The held corpus was searched for the number 11899: the only instruments acting on it are Executive Orders 12107 and 12608; the 1989 codification line, the U.S. Code note and the current 5 CFR part 352 authority lines recite the order as amended and do not revoke it. No held instrument amends, revokes or supersedes it beyond those two. Current predicate: the U.S. Code note under 25 U.S.C. 5323 (release point 119-121, in the packet) prints the order as amended by Executive Orders 12107 and 12608 with the references updated to 25 U.S.C. 5323; 25 U.S.C. 5323(i), the successor of section 105(i) of the Act, still provides that the President may prescribe regulations to carry out subsections (e) to (h) (repository-held Code text, not cited as evidence); and 5 CFR part 352 (repository-held CFR text) cites the order in its authority line. Bounded searches read against their coverage notes: current-law:usc (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk XML; two hits, 5 CFR part 352) and later-events:ofr_catalog (two hits, Executive Orders 12107 and 12608). Limit disclosed for section 2: the command to issue reemployment regulations has no deadline, and no packet source dates when the Commission or the Office of Personnel Management first issued them, so the clause is not recorded as exhausted by performance; the current 5 CFR part 352 authority line shows the regulations are maintained under the order.
